questions.q: Which line must appear at the top of a .c file that calls printf or scanf?
questions.explain: printf and scanf are part of C's standard I/O library. You include it with #include <stdio.h>.

questions.q: Like Python's print, C's printf automatically prints a newline at the end of its output.
questions.explain: printf prints only what the format string contains. To end the line you have to put \n at the end of the format string yourself.

questions.q: For each placeholder (such as %d) in printf's format string, printf expects one additional argument after the format string.
questions.explain: Each placeholder is filled by the next argument in order, so there should be one argument per placeholder.

questions.q: What is wrong with this statement?   printf("%d and %d\n", 7);
choices: The second %d placeholder has no matching argument
\n is not allowed inside a format string
%d cannot appear twice in one format string
Nothing; printf reuses 7 for both placeholders
questions.explain: printf expects one extra argument for every placeholder. There are two %d placeholders here but only one argument.

questions.q: In a printf format string, what does \t print?
questions.explain: \t is a special character that prints a tab. \n prints a newline.

questions.q: num1 is 30 and num2 is 67. What does this print?   printf("%d + %d = %d\n", num1, num2, (num1+num2));
questions.explain: The three %d placeholders are filled in order with num1 (30), num2 (67), and the value of num1+num2 (97).

questions.q: Which placeholder is used to print an int value?
questions.explain: %d is the placeholder for a decimal value (int, short, char).

questions.q: Which of these placeholders prints a float (or double) value?
questions.explain: %g is a placeholder for a float or double value, as in printf("Ht: %g\n", 5.9);

questions.q: Fill in the blank with the placeholder that makes this print Name: Vijay   printf("Name: ___\n", "Vijay");
questions.explain: %s is the placeholder for a string value.

questions.q: Which of these types can be printed as a decimal number with the %d placeholder?
questions.explain: %d is the placeholder for a decimal value: int, short, or char. Strings use %s and doubles use %g.

questions.q: char ch = 'A';   printf("%d\n", ch);   What number is printed?
questions.explain: %d prints the char's numeric value. 'A' is stored as its ASCII value, 65.

questions.q: char ch = 99;   printf("%c\n", ch);   What is printed?
choices: Nothing; %c only works with a character literal like 'c'
questions.explain: %c prints the ASCII character that the value encodes, and 99 is the encoding of lowercase 'c'.

questions.q: Given char ch = 'A';   what does printf("%c is %d\n", ch, ch); print?
questions.explain: The same value is printed twice: as a character with %c (A) and as a number with %d (65).

questions.q: What does the %c placeholder print?
choices: The ASCII character that a numeric value encodes
The numeric value of a character
The number of characters in a string
questions.explain: %c prints a value as a character, for example the ASCII character that matches a numeric encoding. %d would print the number instead.

questions.q: Which statement correctly reads an int typed by the user into the int variable count?
questions.explain: The format string comes first. It is followed by the location of the variable where the value should be stored, which you get by writing &count.

questions.q: How many values does this call read in?   scanf("%d%g", &x, &pi);
questions.explain: The format string sets how many values are read and their types: %d is one int and %g is one float.

questions.q: Which declarations match this call?   scanf("%d%g", &x, &pi);
questions.explain: %d reads an int into x and %g reads a float into pi.

questions.q: scanf is robust to badly formed user input and accepts values typed in almost any format.
questions.explain: scanf can be picky about the exact format of the input, so it does not handle badly formed input well.

questions.q: Badly formed input to scanf has sent a program into an infinite loop. Which key combination stops the program?
questions.explain: Pressing CTRL-C terminates a running program.

questions.q: In scanf("%d", &num1);   what does &num1 produce?
choices: A logical AND of num1 and the input
questions.explain: Putting & in front of a variable name gives the variable's location in memory. scanf stores the value it reads at that address.

questions.q: What is the bug in this code?   int num1;   scanf("%d", num1);
choices: It should pass &num1 so scanf gets the variable's location
%d should be %s because keyboard input is text
The format string needs a \n at the end
num1 must be declared as a float
questions.explain: scanf needs the locations of the variables it fills in, so the argument has to be &num1, not num1.

questions.q: The arguments after scanf's format string give the locations of the variables where the values read in will be stored.
questions.explain: scanf's arguments are memory locations such as &x, not values, because scanf writes the input into those variables.

questions.q: int x; float pi;   scanf("%d%g", &x, &pi);   Which of these typed inputs store 8 in x and 3.14 in pi?
choices: several spaces, then 8, then many more spaces, then 3.14
questions.explain: Numeric input values must be separated by at least one whitespace character. scanf skips any extra spaces, tabs, or newlines before and after each value. In '83.14' there is nothing separating the two values, and a comma is not whitespace.

questions.q: To read two numbers typed with a space between them, scanf's format string must have a space between the placeholders, as in "%d %g" rather than "%d%g".
questions.explain: scanf skips leading and trailing whitespace when it reads a numeric value, so "%d%g" works. The format string is usually just a sequence of placeholders.

questions.q: When typing numeric input for scanf, what must separate two values?
choices: At least one whitespace character (space, tab, or newline)
Nothing; scanf splits the digits automatically
questions.explain: The values must be separated by at least one whitespace character. Because scanf skips extra whitespace, any amount of it works.

questions.q: Newlines count as whitespace that scanf skips over when reading numeric values.
questions.explain: Spaces, tabs, and newlines are all whitespace, and scanf skips them before and after numeric values.

questions.q: How does reading an integer from the user differ between Python and C?
choices: Python's input returns a string that must be converted with int(); C's scanf reads an int and stores it at a variable's memory location
Python's input returns an int directly; C's scanf returns a string that must be converted
Both read a string that the program must convert to an int
C can only read strings from the keyboard, not numbers
questions.explain: Python reads a string and then converts it with int(). C's scanf with %d reads an int and stores it straight into the variable, for example at &num1.

questions.q: Which C statement produces the same output as Python's   print("\tAge: %d" % 20)
questions.explain: C's printf needs an explicit \n because Python's print adds one automatically. In C the arguments follow the format string after a comma, not after %, and an int uses %d.

questions.q: C and Python use different formatting placeholders for the same types of values.
questions.explain: C uses the same formatting placeholders as Python, such as %d, %g, and %s. What differs is how the argument values are listed.
